name: Scanner sweep
description: A hand-held sensor passed slowly over a wall and back, 1.5 s. The scanner's beam is heard as air ringing in a narrow tube whose length changes with the sweep: the hollow tone glides from 320 Hz up to 1.9 kHz at 750 ms and back down, fluttering 21 times a second like scan lines. At the top of the sweep, when the beam crosses something, it pings (a small glassy FM note) and the ping echoes twice inside the device.

tracks.note: The sweep: noise ringing in a tube resonator whose pitch follows the hand. Odd harmonics make it hollow, which reads as a beam rather than a synth.
The find: lands where the sweep turns round. The delay is the device's own little echo.

controls.label: Sweep speed
controls.hint: A slow careful pass to a quick flick.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big deep-scan unit to a small shrill one.

controls.label: Scan lines
controls.hint: A smooth beam to a hard, buzzing flicker.

controls.label: Focus
controls.hint: A breathy wide beam to a tight whistling one.

controls.label: Ping
controls.hint: Nothing found, or a clear echoing contact.
